sources.title: Immigration and visas: No Visa Required schedule
sources.publisher: Embassy of Panama in the United States
sources.officialityEvidence: Panama's live Embassy page publishes a nationality schedule headed ‘No Visa Required’, states a three-month maximum, and directly names these five ordinary-passport nationalities.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Denmark, Dominica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Estonia

sources.title: Immigration and visas: Authorized Visas schedule
sources.publisher: Embassy of Panama in the United States
sources.officialityEvidence: Panama's live Embassy schedule expressly places Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Oman, Rwanda and Usbekistan in the authorized-visa cohort, and says not to travel until the visa has been granted. Its Korea label is not used to classify DPRK passports.
sources.supportingExcerpt: you will need an authorized visa

sources.title: Consular services: processing stamped and authorized visas
sources.officialityEvidence: Panama's current Foreign Ministry page explains that a consul grants an authorized visa only after National Migration Service authorization, establishing an advance, not border-issued, instrument.
sources.supportingExcerpt: el Cónsul puede otorgar una visa al solicitante previa autorización del Servicio Nacional de Migración

policies.title: Panama: named ordinary passports visa-free for short visitors
policies.summary: Panama's current Embassy nationality schedule expressly places Andorra, Barbados, Belarus, Denmark and Jamaica in its No Visa Required cohort.
conditions: Applies to ordinary passports from the named nationalities for short visitor travel.
The live schedule gives a maximum stay of three months.
Work, residence, transit, diplomatic or special passports, and final admission are outside this classification.

policies.title: Panama: named ordinary passports requiring an authorized visitor visa
policies.summary: Panama's live Embassy schedule places Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Oman, Rwanda and Usbekistan in the authorized-visa cohort; current Foreign Ministry guidance confirms National Migration authorization precedes consular grant.
conditions: Applies to ordinary passports from the named nationalities for short visitor travel.
The authorized visa is an advance instrument: the consular grant follows National Migration Service authorization; the Embassy cautions against travel until granted.
Excludes the separate conditional waiver for holders of qualifying third-country visas or residence documents.
Work, residence, transit, diplomatic or special passports, and final admission are outside this classification.

unresolved.reason: Panama's live official schedule does not directly name an ordinary Macao SAR passport. No status is inferred from its China row, an omission, or the conditional third-country-document waiver.
No current Panamanian primary source directly maps an ordinary Timor-Leste passport to a short-visitor instrument and actual issuance timing; omission and conditional-waiver inference are excluded.
Panama's schedule names Sudan but not South Sudan. That distinction does not establish an ordinary South Sudan passport's visitor baseline, and no complement or conditional waiver is inferred.

Panama's schedule uses the label ‘People's Republic of Korea’, which does not directly identify a Democratic People's Republic of Korea ordinary passport. This naming ambiguity is not resolved by inference.
